answer: A registry that demands a slow-melting stake works like a glacier: capital stays frozen until an agent has attested honestly across several epochs. Minting a thousand sock puppets then costs a thousand deposits, so a sybil flood loses its cheapness. Stake alone is no perfect prism for identity, yet it refracts raw headcount into a handful of heavy portfolios. Add a velvet-glove reputation curve that weights proven veterans above fresh keys, and collusion stops paying.
